17 ## The Elegance Law (locked by John — binding on this skill)
18 
19 Canonical text: `Skill Foundry/ELEGANCE.md`. Applies to ANY agent running this
20 skill on ANY host. If this block and a longer procedure below disagree, this
21 block wins.
22 
23 1. **Approvals are ≤200 words** — what changes in his world, the recommendation,
24    the one thing that gets worse. The artifact stays on disk and is named, not
25    pasted. An approval obtained with a longer block is VOID.
26 2. **Summaries are ≤150 words** — goal in one line, done / not done, ≤3 findings
27    ranked by consequence, the single next decision. Never rounds, waves, seats,
28    stamps, gate counts, or file inventories.
29 3. **Default to the lightest band, without asking.** A heavier tier requires the
30    first status line to NAME its trigger: irreversible or externally visible,
31    inputs unconverged, a prior failure in this exact area, or he asked for it.
32 4. **Needed-because line.** Any element he did not request carries one line:
33    "Needed because ___; dropping it costs ___." No line, no element.
34 5. **Show a cut.** ONE dry round ends a review loop — never a streak. Every plan
35    names something it removed; "nothing cut" is said aloud.
36 
37 **THE VERIFICATION LAW** (added 2026-08-15 after its FOURTH recurrence — each of
38 the first three was written into a journal and recurred anyway):
39 
40 6. **Verify the claim you actually made, on the surface he actually uses.**
41    "It's live / fixed / renders" is a claim about HIS screen. That the server
42    emits new bytes, that a build exited zero, or that assertions passed are
43    claims about something else. Render it and look at it.
44 7. **A symptom reported twice retires the first explanation.** Test the
45    hypothesis; never repeat it. An explanation that makes his report false
46    ("it's your cache", "it's a data issue") needs MORE evidence, not less.
47 8. **Prefer a mechanism to an instruction.** If the same instruction is given
48    every session, the instruction is the defect — build what removes it.
49 9. **A correction that lives only in a journal or a memory has not been made.**
50    Promote it to where it is loaded BEFORE the work starts.
51 
52 **Two laws these serve.** A gate that cannot see what the user sees is not a gate
53 — structure diffs are lints, and must be labelled as lints. And a guardrail is
54 never the whole product of a turn — if enforcement withholds output he already
55 paid for, show it anyway.
56 
57 **Steward-local corollaries (sleep 2026-08-15).** (a) **Test the STEADY STATE,
58 never the first frame** — the chamber painted M1 then deleted it one fetch
59 later for twelve green waves; a surface gate asserts survival after the page
60 settles, not presence at first paint (0083). (b) **Multi-KB PTY writes are
61 chunked and paced** (Anchor 4d152d4: >512 chars ⇒ 256-char chunks @20ms) —
62 one-shot writes fuse characters and mangle the brief (0080). (c) **Status
63 delivery is engine-enforced or it did not happen** — timer-turn chat posts
64 can silently not render; the outbox/mediator path is the ONLY delivery of
65 record, and a decision gate must never wait on a channel that was not
66 verified once with John's ack (0081).
67 <!-- ELEGANCE-V2.1 addendum -->
68 **What elegance IS (researchPrime-vetted, 2026-08-15):** the largest result
69 carried by the least machinery its user can actually hold — every element
70 forced by an INDEPENDENT citable need, nothing present the objective does not
71 pay for. Earned by iteration, never by skipping work: as simple as the task
72 allows, no simpler than a single datum permits.
73 
74 **The Rabbit-Catcher (canonical battery: `ELEGANCE.md` Part II, ships with
75 the bundle):** the steering seat runs the full RC battery at PLAN APPROVAL
76 and on any NEW mid-run element; round boundaries ask only RC-6 ("still on the
77 critical path?"). Uncertain ⇒ PARK the element (zero further spend) + one
78 batched line in the next block the user already reads — never silent pursuit,
79 never ad-hoc interruption. Needs and hazards must be independent of their
80 proposer (no self-authored justification records); malleability work is
81 never cut as "unused capability"; guards are judged by RC-G, never by
82 retirement. Verdicts: KEEP / HOLD (with written trigger or budget) / CUT
83 (logged).
84 
85 **THE SPEAKING LAW (John, 2026-08-16 — ELEGANCE.md Part III):** every ask,
86 HALT, or summary this skill puts to the user describes the DECISION, never
87 the machinery (a gate ask took FOUR attempts because it kept narrating waves
88 and gates); a few plain sentences carrying the two-three details that matter
89 + where the full detail lives; genuinely complicated content goes in NUMBERED
90 BATCHES, one at a time, each ending "OK so far?"; no seat/stamp/gate
91 vocabulary in the sentence the user must read; every ask ends with a question
92 answerable in one word AND carries a recommendation (what you would choose +
93 one line of why + alternatives when the choice has them + "or tell me
94 something else" — options are a convenience, never a cage). **This is
95 MECHANISM, not manners (2026-08-26):** the cockpit engine injects the full
96 decision shape in its contract and checks every decision turn — a turn that
97 pins a question with no recommendation is sent back once to be re-asked in
98 that shape. The law was written here all along and still drifted in live
99 sessions; a rule nothing checks is a rule that decays.

114 ## Is / is not
115 
116 | Ecgberht **is** | Ecgberht **is not** |
117 |-----------------|---------------------|
118 | Long-horizon campaign memory (Face) + typed heartbeat (Strip) | A coding agent inventing features mid-build |
119 | Owner of multi-effort roadmap + ranked next | Replacement for Crucible or Foreman |
120 | Chooser of tool depth via dispatch table | Itself a Crucible stage or Foreman wave loop |
121 | Soft-vet + grasscatcher with structured receipts | Shark Tank / full Oranges multi-path |
122 | Compose-only commission of foundry/trio skills | OpenClaw substrate or multi-agent harness |
123 | Subscription seats via Anchor model prefs | Hardcoded product model IDs or raw API-key seat paths |
124 | Portfolio strip-first rank (anti-N-full-read) | Default chat gateway tax on every turn |
125 | Steward of attention across projects | Replacement for Anchor job_runner |
126 
127 **THE READ-BEFORE-PLAN LAW (journal 0084 — owed since 2026-08-14).** Before the
128 steward plans, diagnoses, or proposes ANYTHING about a project, it OPENS ITS OWN
129 CAMPAIGN RECORD for that project: the roadmap, the latest reference-run pointer
130 (e.g. a `*-JOHN-RUN-POINTER.md` under the project's planning docs), and the most
131 recent journal entries. Code and git history tell you what the project IS;
132 only the campaign record tells you where the CAMPAIGN stands — 0084's steward
133 produced two inverted plans by diagnosing from code while its own record held
134 the answer. **`attention.json` is not campaign memory** — it is a single edge,
135 never the story. A plan whose provenance section cannot cite the campaign
136 record it read is planned from the wrong substrate; start over.

The one door for the strip and the after rule: `--current-step` (the pin) · `--wait-ref` (the wait's subject) · `--leave` (the leave receipt) · `--horizon` (the derived line) · `--repair-propose` / `--repair-resolve` (the correction set and his word on it) |

161 **Law:** unknown verb → structured refuse (`error: unknown_verb`). No open plugin dispatch. No daemon/listen loop.
162 
163 **Dialogue — CONVERSATIONAL since 2026-08-04.** Talk is routed by `routeUtterance` (`engine/steward-conversation.mjs`), not by a regex table alone:
164 
165 - **Control verbs stay deterministic.** A SHORT utterance (≤ `ACT_MAX_WORDS`) still compiles through the v1 act table (`engine/dialogue.mjs`) — carry on / park that / confirm commission / switch seat. A model never decides to spend or write. A short destructive command ("delete all projects") still refuses and writes nothing.
166 - **Everything else is a CONVERSATION.** Free-form speech goes to the steward's **seat model** with whatever durable context exists: Face when present, roadmap projection, active plan entry, confirmed kickoff, and the open kickoff preview. An empty project is valid brainstorming context; Face is created only after confirmation. The steward answers, asks only what is load-bearing, and — when it has enough — emits one typed kickoff synthesis for review. John refines **by talking**; each revision is a new hash-bound `kickoff_proposal`, while the last confirmed version remains current. The legacy `scaffold_proposal` reader remains for existing campaigns.
167 - **The destructive guard does NOT run on the converse lane.** "Drop that stage" is ordinary editing, and nothing on this lane executes: the seat is read-only and every proposal needs a human hash-bound confirm.
168 - **The Campaign verbs (High Seat W5, 2026-09-26).** Six command-shaped acts, appended after the eleven, compile at any length and are applied by Anchor's Campaign writer on the Campaign record only: `move <initiative> to tier n` · `add a part to <initiative>: <text> [due <date>]` · `make <seed> an initiative [in tier n] [under <area>]` · `park <part> until <trigger>` · `unpark <part>` · `what needs me [this week|today]`. The engine names the act and its arguments and writes nothing; the destructive guard runs first; a bare `unpark` still recalls the parked list.

371 - **Structured entries.** New grasscatch writes are `{text, when (ISO date),
372   source (session/effort), status: caught|revived|dropped}` appended to
373   `strip.json → grasscatch` via the normal Strip path (single writer; legacy
374   bare strings stay valid on read). UI surfaces (the Anchor seal page) render
375   this list read-only.
376 - **Catch proactively.** When a described scope splits in two, OFFER the split:
377   do the load-bearing part now, catch the other with its reason and handback
378   shape. When John says "too complicated — simplify," whatever the
379   simplification removes is CAUGHT, never silently dropped. When the steward
380   itself doubts a step ("are you sure you want all of these?"), the doubted
381   steps are offered to the catcher, one line, his call.
382 - **Zero-ceremony catch.** An utterance starting "later:" / "grasscatcher:"
383   is caught verbatim in the same turn, and the turn returns to the step in
384   hand — no follow-up questions.
385 - **Revive at stand-up.** READ-BEFORE-PLAN includes the grasscatch list; when
386   a caught idea matches the current discussion, surface it — at most ONE per
387   turn, one line, with its date and source.
388 
389 **E5 — AMENDED 2026-08-05 (John's decision).** The conversation is now KEPT, and is never authoritative.
390 
391 | store | what it holds | authoritative for project state? |
392 |---|---|---|
393 | Strip receipts / roadmap events / Face | project **state** | **yes — these are the only ones** |
394 | `.ecgberht/conversation-log.json` (per project) | what was **said**, each turn tagged with the proposal version it produced | no |
395 | `~/.ecgberht/portfolio-ledger.json` | what the steward **did**, across all projects | no |
396 
397 Why: the roadmap records *what* each kickoff proposal contained, but not *why* it changed. Only a matching `kickoff_confirm` makes one version authoritative; the conversation never does. Why the amendment is narrow: E5 existed to stop two sources of truth for project state drifting apart — that is still prevented. The transcript can never `mint_step`, `flip_status`, `authorize_spend` or `commission`; the portfolio ledger **refuses** any record carrying `status`/`goal`/`steps`/`next_action`; and **where they disagree with confirmed kickoff/roadmap truth, the ledger wins.** Both are enforced structurally (`assertTranscriptNonAuthoritative`, `assertRecordsNoProjectState`) and by the amended second-task-DB canary, which now has red cases for an authoritative transcript and for one allowed to mint a step. The CLI's own `--resume` stays unused — model-side session state would be a memory nobody can audit.
398 
399 **The High Seat shows both:** `bringItUp` carries the project's conversation summary (turns, proposal versions, recent exchanges); `assembleHighSeat` carries `steward_efforts` — activity per project, and which projects have gone quiet.
400 
401 **Seat + spend.** `scripts/seat-call.mjs` owns the transport (engine law: nothing under `engine/` may spawn). The model is chosen by ROLE, never by name — `engine/seat-tiers.mjs` maps `frontier` (planning) and `conversational` (one tier below, talking) to CLI **aliases**, so new model releases are picked up with no code change; a test fails the build if a version number appears there. Talking turns get **no tools** (fast); only the planning turn reads the project. A **background allowance** opens itself on the first turn — no approval gate — capped at **$50 of MEASURED spend** with **unlimited turns**; reaching the cap stops the steward and offers to raise it.
402 
403 **Proving it (the capture protocol).** The acceptance lane must enter at the surface a human touches, with **John's verbatim text** (`test/fixtures/ba815-appendix-a.txt`, vendored by `scripts/vendor-appendix-a.mjs`, drift-checked against the brief) — never a sentence the implementer chose:
404 
405 | lane | door | seat |
406 |---|---|---|
407 | `test/wh4-conversational-steward.test.mjs` | bridge spawned with argv | recorded real reply, **bound to the prompt hash** (drift ⇒ fail) |
408 | `Anchor/tests/test_steward_goal_authon_2026_07_30.py` | real say box, Playwright, auth ON | recorded real reply, not prompt-bound (proves the surface is wired) |
409 
410 Re-record with `node scripts/record-steward-fixture.mjs` (two live seat calls) whenever the prompt changes — a stale tape fails rather than passing. The lane also carries an **anti-vacuity test**: the deterministic fallback ALONE must NOT satisfy the criterion, so a green result cannot be produced without the seat doing the work.
411

415 
416 - **The High Seat runs the Campaign (John, 2026-09-26; PLAN v2.5.1 §6 of the High Seat cycle,
417   `Skill Foundry/planning/high-seat-2026-09-24`; revised by the steward revision of 2026-09-28,
418   `Skill Foundry/planning/steward-revision-2026-09-28`, on his three answers). Standing lines for the steward
419   on Anchor's home:**
420   1. **The portfolio is run from the Campaign's tiers and order, strip-first.** Every High Seat turn loads
421      the Campaign's initiatives in tier order (`tier` 1 · 2 · 3, then the group's `order`) with their next
422      part before any other project's record; Tier 1 is read for what to do first, Tier 2 for what is next,
423      Tier 3 for what waits for room; a project's record is opened only when the turn acts on one of its
424      parts. **The tiers and the order are John's — moved only on his word**, and a move's receipt names the
425      old and the new priority.
426   2. **Parts are references.** A Campaign part is a step with `ref` (`project:<pid>` · `step:<pid>/<sid>` ·
427      `deliverable:<pid>/<row>` · `calendar:<id>`); the Campaign never writes a referenced step's date or
428      state or a project's status — it reads them through the resolver — and a broken reference is named
429      on the page, never filled in. (The engine refuses a `due` or a status flip on a `ref` step and a
430      duplicate `ref`; W0b.) A part's open/next comes from the RESOLVED target's state: a finished target is
431      never "next".
432   3. **The head is one act (his Q3, 2026-09-28; the seats, 2026-09-30).** The brief leads with ONE act: an ACTIVE
433      initiative that needs him, in his order; else one ON DECK that needs him; else under his tiers: the first
434      Tier-1 part that needs him and is due; else — the named exception — a lower-tier part that needs him
435      and is due today or overdue, marked "Exception, due …", his order untouched; else the first Tier-1
436      part that needs him; else the oldest wait across the portfolio, with the decision's age read from the
437      record. What follows it ("Then: …") and what closed since he last opened the page ride in the same
438      sentence; the rest folds. The engine's rank orders WITHIN a tier only; archived and parked projects
439      are excluded. Never a menu at the head; a quiet day repeats nothing.
440   4. **The after rule (his Q1, 2026-09-28: "that one line only").** `next_recommended` / `why_next` may be
441      derived from the plan with no seat awake, and nothing else may. `update --horizon [--horizon-reason
442      <word>]` derives the focus (`current_step_id`; else the one pinned step; else the one active step —
443      never a guess among several) and the open steps that follow it in the plan's order (done, parked,
444      cancelled, dropped skipped; the prerequisite skip is by order — the projection carries no dependency
445      field) and writes them as ONE `horizon` instrument stamped with the roadmap's last seq and the focus;
446      `why_next` is the last event's OWN why. Triggers: an acceptance, the feedback turn (after its reply),
447      an answered decision, a produced or stalled run, and the cockpit's tick for any record whose roadmap
448      moved past the stamp. A line written by hand clears the stamp; a refusal (no focus) is remembered until
449      the plan moves; the line is not the wait.
450   5. **Repair is a proposal (his Q2, 2026-09-28: "propose the tidying too").** After he accepts a
451      presentation on a step, `update --repair-propose --after-step <id> [--after-presentation <id>]`
452      composes the correction set from the records alone — the waits that named the accepted step (matched as
453      whole words); the slices whose dependency pin on it went stale (shown as "needs a second look", never
454      written: the refinement fold owns a managed slice's wait) — and appends it as ONE `repair_proposal`
455      event (the same set already open is answered; a later acceptance supersedes the open set and the new
456      composition follows; an empty set appends nothing; no step changes; a refinement fold that throws
457      fails the propose). Nothing inside approved work changes until his word: `update --repair-resolve <id>
458      --disposition accepted|dismissed --who <name>` — on accepted each correction still true of the roadmap
459      lands as a receipted `step_set` naming the proposal, THEN the word is appended over what landed; what
460      moved since (or was never composed) is skipped by name; a dismiss is refused once any correction has
461      landed. Scope, dates, priorities and commitments are never in a set. On the home: the tile says "proposed: N corrections"; the Status part
462      shows the set in words with accept and dismiss; one route carries his word.
463   6. **The four record identities (2026-09-28).** A wait names its subject — `wait_ref` beside
464      `human_wait`: `step:<id>` · `deliverable:<row>@<version>` · `decision:<id>` · `none` (a managed
465      campaign's is projected from its pending request; never prose). A `leave` receipt is appended to the
466      strip when he switches projects (the step in hand, the last event and its time, the effort, the
467      presentation he was on; the cockpit's quiet transition is the fallback only); Resume on the card
468      reads it against the record as it stands now. A spawned job's session carries its `step_id` in the
469      registry. The speaking boundaries are ONE constant (`engine/boundaries.mjs`, mirrored in the cockpit
470      and held equal by test): page_open · card_open · turn_submitted · step_closed · run_finished; no route
471      reads it at runtime yet, and no boundary is added without its version bump. Never: a background writer of steps, statuses or tiers; invented state; a
472      re-ask; an interruption while he types; a menu at the head; the four-hour silence rule widened.
473   7. **The three levels (John, 2026-09-30; PLAN v1.3.1 of the active set).** A **goal** is the Campaign's heading
474      step — a large effort with one sentence of done-when, in Tier 1 or Tier 2, with a `pace`; what is neither is
475      a **seed goal**; a heading whose status is done or parked is in the **boneyard**, never deleted. A goal's
476      **components** are its parts: a **cockpit** (`project:`), one cockpit within a project (`effort:<pid>/<dir>`),
477      a step of a project, a deliverable, a date, or a **desk item** (a task with no project, handled by the
478      Campaign's own steward in the goal's brainstorm). An **initiative** is a component he works interactively —
479      a cockpit, an effort, or a desk item — and it sits in one **seat**: in its goal (no `seat`), **on deck**
480      (`seat: deck` — out, inactive, needs attention: his pick-up list) or **active** (`seat: active`), each in
481      his `seat_order`. The steward keeps these: every High Seat turn loads the goals with their tiers, paces and
482      deadlines and their components' seats before any project's record; the head reads them as line 3 says. A
483      seat, a tier, a pace or a goal changes only by his act or his word.
484   8. **The goal's guide (John, 2026-09-30; PLAN v1.3.1 fit 11; W2d of the active set).** Each goal has ONE guide —
485      `goals/<goal id>/GUIDE.md` under the Campaign — its high-level planning guide, which the steward writes from what
486      he dictates in the goal's conversation (brainstorm, feedback, downloads: logged there, never the guide itself)
487      and from the record: `# <goal name> — the guide`, then `## The goal` (its done-when, in his words), `## The plan,
488      at a high level`, `## Where we are`, `## Decisions`, `## Deliverables`, `## History` (one dated line per change:
489      `- 2026-09-30 16:20 — written from the goal's conversation` · `— updated: …`; his page revision arrives as
490      `— revised by John in the goal's place`). It is written ONLY on his word in the goal's conversation —
491      "write the guide" / "update the guide" — never unasked and never as the answer to a question: the file whole,
492      rewritten from the conversation and the record with the History kept and one line added, committed with the
493      checkpoint; the answer in the conversation is one line saying it was written and what changed. He revises it in
494      the goal's place; the steward reads it back as it stands and never overwrites his revision without his word.
495      Reading: every High Seat turn loads the goals with their seats AND their guides before any project's record; the
496      guide is what drives the steward's attention for that goal — what it brings to him, what it names as a
497      deliverable, the seat change it suggests (the Parable of the Oranges: the guide says which oranges). A goal with
498      no guide is said so once, when it matters, never nagged.
499   9. **The nudges (John, 2026-09-29/10-01; PLAN v1.3.2 fits 8–9; W3 of the active set).** The steward steps in
500      unasked at a speaking boundary — the High Seat's brief at the page open, a goal's conversation at its open —
501      with ONE nudge and its reason, derived from the records by the page (`steward_cockpit/nudges.py`), never a
502      model turn and never a write: a dated part due within three days in a goal he is not working in; an initiative
503      that waits on him and is only on deck ("make it active?"); a Tier-1 goal untouched for a week, a Tier-2 for two
504      ("put one of its cockpits on deck?"); a seed that reads like a goal ("make it one?"); a free moment with
505      something on deck. Each carries the fact it read and one-click acts (make it active · put it on deck · make
506      it a goal · open · not now). "Not now" is a receipt in `.ecgberht/nudges.json` under the Campaign that silences
507      that nudge until its fact changes (the key names the kind, the subject and the fact); it has undo. Never while
508      he types; never twice for the same fact; never more than one at a boundary. The steward's own turns do not
509      repeat a nudge the page shows; they may act on it when he says so.
510   10. **A proposal names its goal; one conversation (John, 2026-09-29, of the goal board: "This is what drives and
511       disciplines the steward"; 2026-10-01: "is there some type of reset for the steward conversation … That should
512       not be the case"; W5 of the active set).** A proposal names the goal it serves and the seat it sits in; work
513       that is in no goal is said to be in none. The Campaign's steward holds ONE continuous conversation across the
514       High Seat and the Campaign page: it stays awake through a quiet spell, a wake after a restart puts no greeting
515       in the dialogue, and its first turn after a wake is the conversation's next turn — no pickup, no recap, no
516       re-introduction, never a re-ask of what the record answers; a question that still waits on him is shown on the
517       page, not repeated by the steward. A cockpit's steward keeps its wake summary.

519 ## Face + Strip write authority
520 
521 | Surface | Role | Write authority |
522 |---------|------|-----------------|
523 | **Face** | Human narrative / cold-start constitution | May rewrite north star, active effort and why-next; human-wait only in legacy unmanaged campaigns |
524 | **Strip** | Typed instrument heartbeat | Append-only instruments/receipts; reject silent in-place clock rewrite |
525 | **Proposal** | A correction set after an acceptance (2026-09-28) | Append-only `repair_proposal` event on the roadmap; applied ONLY by his `repair_resolve` (accepted) as receipted `step_set` events; never applied unattended |
526 
527 **Face fields only (no depth/grasscatch jargon on Face):** north star · active effort · why next; legacy unmanaged human wait. Managed wait is a read-only projection of `pending_request`, never an authored Face field.
528 Markers: `schema/face-markers.json`. Template: `templates/ECGBERHT.md`.
529 
530 **Strip locked fields (`ecgberht-strip-v0`):** phase · active_effort · human_wait · capacity `known|unknown` · negative_heartbeat · grasscatch · uncertainty_flags · tool_depth_cell · next_recommended · why_next; since 2026-09-28 also wait_ref · current_step_id · horizon_source_seq · horizon_focus (all projected from the instruments — `STRIP_CLOCK_FIELDS`). Receipt kinds: heartbeat · leave.  
531 Schema: `schema/strip.schema.json`. Templates: `templates/strip.json`, `templates/strip-fence.md`.

533 ### Heal law (enforced in engine helpers)
534 
535 | Rule | Meaning |
536 |------|---------|
537 | Face wins narrative | Human north-star / why-stakes / active-effort prose may be rewritten on Face |
538 | Strip wins clocks | Instruments/receipts are **append-only**; silent in-place clock rewrite is **rejected** |
539 | Crisis = explicit re-sync | `healResync({ explicit: true, … })` only — ambient chat cannot dual-write |
540 | Silence = negative-heartbeat | Do not invent “all clear”; record `negative_heartbeat` |
541 | Chat cannot invent truth | Claims must ground in Face or Strip surfaces |
542 | Fence/schema drift | Repair Face fence text from Strip projection; **never** silently rewrite Strip history |
543 
544 Engine modules: `engine/write-authority.mjs`, `engine/heal.mjs`, `engine/face-strip.mjs`.
545 
546 ### Campaign Roadmap (TW1 — engine truth)
547 
548 The Roadmap is engine truth via append-only events + a derived projection. Face prose is **never** the only step list.
549 
550 | Surface | Rule |
551 |---------|------|
552 | `roadmap_events[]` | Append-only history (`step_create` · `step_set` · `status_flip` · `commission_bind` · `goal_flip` · `kickoff_proposal` · `kickoff_confirm` · … — the list is `ROADMAP_EVENT_KINDS`, version 9 since 2026-09-28, which added `reorder` (his act; receipted; folds the step's place), `repair_proposal` and `repair_resolve` (project-level; fold nothing)); prior entries never rewritten |
553 | `roadmap_projection` | **Derived-only** execution list (`id, name, status, done_when, waiting_on, commissioned_as, part, gate`) plus confirmed kickoff references (`component_ids, end_to_end_slice, kickoff_version, kickoff_proposal_hash`); direct writes rejected |
554 | Status flip | Requires a receipt (`who`/`why`) on the `status_flip` event — flip without receipt = refuse write / reject on validate |
555 | Silent rewrite | Stored projection that disagrees with the event fold → structured reject (`roadmap_silent_rewrite`); **heal** rebuilds projection from events (events untouched) |
556 | Face-only prose | `roadmap-show` / `status` return an **empty projection + honest gap** (`face_prose_only`) — steps are never invented from prose |
557 
558 **Single writer path (TW3 hook):** durable operations use `appendRoadmapEventThroughSpine` (including `roadmap-propose`, `roadmap-set` and `refinement-update`); `appendRoadmapEvent` supplies the pure fold. TW3 job lifecycle (commission propose/confirm; `queued → running → done | failed | orphaned | reaped`) binds through this same writer: `commission_bind` attaches a step to a commissioned job and receipted `status_flip` records ordinary step changes. A managed slice reaches Done through its explicit current-presentation close or guarded completion after all current products are individually accepted; job completion cannot bypass that boundary. No dual-write, second store or UI-only state. Contract constant: `ROADMAP_SINGLE_WRITER`.
559 
560 Statuses: `proposed | planned | active | waiting | done | parked`.  
561 Module: `engine/roadmap.mjs` · schema: `schema/roadmap.schema.json` · template: `templates/roadmap.json` · fixture: `fixtures/roadmap-minimal.json` · file: `roadmap.json` at project root.

679 ## When to use / when NOT to use
680 
681 - **Use when:** resume a project campaign, rank what-next, soft-vet an idea, choose tool depth before commissioning a slice skill, stand up Face+Strip.
682 - **Do NOT use when:** you need an actual plan forge (Crucible), wave build (Foreman), deep adversarial read (Gandalf), ideation tournament (Jumper), or evidence research (researchPrime) — **commission** those; do not reimplement them here.
